nonBlocking.title: Reading of the owner decision — counting unary operations is the safer of the two readings, and costs this crate nothing
nonBlocking.detail: The decision text says 'one binary operation, no Parens'; the code counts unaries too (src/authorize.rs:534-538). The narrower reading (one binary plus any unaries) would re-admit divergent reprints: `[true, false, Equal, Negate]` prints `!true === false` and reparses as `(!true) === false` (parser.rs:366-376, `!` binds expr6), `[2, 3, Mul, TypeOf, …]` prints `2 * 3.type()` and reparses with `.type()` bound to `3`; under the strict reading both are refused (`R3 [precedence-!(true===false)] -> DENY(auth.biscuit_invalid)`, `R3 [precedence-(2*3).type()] -> DENY`). What the strict reading refuses in addition is faithful two-operation shapes: `!true === false` written as `[true, Negate, false, Equal]`, `{,}.length() === 0`, `6 & 3 === 2`, `$x.length() === 4` (all DENY(auth.biscuit_invalid) in the probe, all FAITHFUL). Neither reading refuses anything `attenuate()` emits — src/token.rs attenuation_block writes four checks with at most one operation each (`{operations}.contains($operation)`, `$time < {expires_at}`), and `holder_expressions_with_a_single_operation_stay_accepted` plus the 57-test suite hold. A single unary alone stays admissible (`!false` -> ACCEPT | FAITHFUL; `!1`, `{1}.length()`, `1.type()` -> DENY(auth.operation_denied) by the evaluator, FAITHFUL). Verdict on the interpretation: safer, not neutral, not harmful within this crate; harmful only to a hand-built holder block that needs `.length()`/`.type()`/`!` combined with a comparison, which SECURITY.md:159-160 and :210-216 now say.
